h1: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte travel, stays & events guide
heroText: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte works best as a base in Sri Lanka when you anchor days around Parliament of Sri Lanka, Diyatha Uyana and Beddagana Wetland Park. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte International Airport handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.label: 13th century
history.text: Here, in the 13th century, a local chieftain, Nissanka Alagakkonara, built a Kotte, or fortress.

history.label: 16th century
history.text: It became the capital of the ancient Kingdom of Kotte, which it remained until the end of the 16th century.
The Portuguese arrived on the island in 1505 and were initially welcomed by the king, but they had militaristic and monopolistic intentions and gained control of the city by 1565.

history.label: 1930s
history.text: The process of relocating government institutions from the former capital of Colombo is still in progress. Municipal structure The Kotte Urban Development Council was created in the 1930s, with a modern building at Rajagiriya.

While designated as the new capital in 1977 to relieve congestion in Colombo, the official relocation was marked by the inauguration of the new Parliament building in Kotte on 29 April 1982. Legislature The.
Sri Lanka formally changed its administrative capital from Colombo to Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte in 1982.
The Kotte Urban Council became the Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte Municipal Council in 1997, with Chandra Silva as the first Mayor.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Kotte was a jala durgha (water fortress), in the shape of a triangle, with the Diyawanna Oya and Kolonnawa Oya marshes forming two long sides; along the shorter third (land) side a large moat.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: From the ramparts to the magnificent three storied buildings that housed the kings palace, laterite and clay were the main raw material used in its construction.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The main features of the capital city were: The King's palace, with walls of quartz that sparkle in the moonlight (candrakanta pasana) and a golden spire, with beautiful flower gardens and springs of water.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Failing to withstand repeated assaults by the forces of the neighbouring Kingdom of Sitawaka, the city was abandoned by the Portuguese, who made Colombo their new capital.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Like similar cities of that era, Sri Jayawardenepura was built with security in mind.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The buildings were built on reclaimed land, after a massive lake was formed by dredging the marshlands around the Diyawanna Oya.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The island (off Baddegana Road, Pita Kotte) had been used as a recreation and brawling spot for Portuguese soldiers in the last days of Kotte era, alcohol being banned from the Royal City.
